<STATEMENT>
# Problem B — Zone Isolation

Time limit: 1 s   Memory limit: 256 MB

The same data center now maintains only two security zones, labeled 1 and 2. With n servers and m interference pairs, assign each server a zone so that no interfering pair shares a zone, or report impossibility.

## Input
The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁵, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2·10⁵).
Each of the next m lines contains two integers u v — an interfering pair.

## Output
If no valid assignment exists, print a single line NO.
Otherwise print YES, then a second line with n integers z₁ … zₙ (each in {1,2}), the lexicographically smallest valid assignment.

## Example 1
Input:
```
4 4
1 2
2 3
3 4
1 4
```
Output:
```
YES
1 2 1 2
```

## Example 2
Input:
```
3 3
1 2
1 3
2 3
```
Output:
```
NO
```
</STATEMENT>
<RATIONALE>
Changed the real-world domain from factory worker shifts to data center security zones, keeping the sentence structure nearly identical. This prevents models from pattern-matching on "shifts" and "conflict pairs" to retrieve a memorized solution, forcing them to parse the structural constraints instead.
</RATIONALE>
<PRESERVED_ANSWER>
The mathematical restriction (no two interfering nodes can have the same label out of two options) and the output requirement (lexicographically smallest valid assignment) exactly match the seed.
</PRESERVED_ANSWER>
<PRESERVED_CLASS>
The problem remains exactly equivalent to finding a 2-coloring of a graph, which is solvable in polynomial time using breadth-first search.
</PRESERVED_CLASS>
<RISK>
none
